The largest numerical risk is treating relayed exit codes 129–192 as proof of a signal even though the wrapper relays any explicit evaluator exit code unchanged.

reviewers.summary: Round 3 correctly reads signal death from exit status, but the shared-stderr demotion still keys off `rc == 0`, which can never fire for the evaluator's intentional `sys.exit(-1)` crash paths. Combined with the newly working padded-`Aborted` patterns, ordinary self-terminated `Simulation crashed` / `Agent couldn't be set up` records are misrouted onto the killed axis and can change settled statuses after the extra retries.

findings.title: Demotion uses rc==0, so intentional exit-255 crash verdicts with CARLA stderr faults become FAULT/killed
findings.evidence:
signalled = reap.describe_exit_signal(rc)
hard = fault or signalled
...
clean_exit = rc == 0

if clean_exit and has_record:
    attempt.outcome = AttemptOutcome.EXITED  # demotion
elif has_record:
    attempt.outcome = AttemptOutcome.FAULT
findings.why_wrong: The vendored evaluator's crashed=True paths (Simulation crashed; Agent couldn't be set up; sensors invalid) always end in sys.exit(-1) → rc 255. describe_exit_signal(255) correctly returns None (not a signal). Demotion requires rc == 0, so it is unreachable for those statuses. Round 3 also made Aborted\s+(core dumped) match the shell's padded column, so Simulation crashed / Agent_init self-terminations that print a normal UE4 abort line—exactly the population that used to miss the dead one-space pattern and fall through to EXITED→record—now become FAULT→ABNORMAL_END→killed. That spends killed_budget (default 2) and re-runs routes whose self-terminated verdict should have charged record; a retry can settle a different status. Signal deaths remain distinguishable via signalled; rc == 0 is a too-narrow proxy for not signalled.
findings.suggested_fix: Demote on has_record and fault and signalled is None (process exited with a non-signal status), not on rc == 0. Keep FAULT whenever describe_exit_signal(rc) is set. Optionally stop consulting FAULT_PATTERNS for post-exit classification entirely and use them only for the in-flight kill branch.

findings.title: Relayed exit codes can misclassify intentional evaluator exits as hard deaths
findings.evidence: `describe_exit_signal` treats `128 < rc <= 128 + _MAX_SIGNAL` as `killed by ...`, while the generated wrapper does `rc=$?` followed by `exit ${rc}`.
findings.why_wrong: An evaluator that intentionally exits 134, 139, or another value in that range is indistinguishable from a shell-relayed signal. LocalBackend then classifies a final retryable record as FAULT and charges the bounded killed axis instead of the model record axis, changing retries and potentially the settled result.
findings.suggested_fix: Use an explicit signal marker/trap or another side channel for shell-relayed deaths; do not infer signal death from the numeric exit range alone.

findings.title: Dry-run still writes settlement and ledger mutations
findings.evidence: Planning mutates `st.finished` for `SKIP_DONE`, `SKIP_EXHAUSTED`, and `RUN`, then calls `state.save()`. The final rollback restores only `attempts_infra` from `infra_clear_undo` before another unconditional `state.save()`.
findings.why_wrong: `--dry-run` can create task entries, change settlement bits, and overwrite the stored config digest despite claiming that nothing was written. In particular, previewing a changed config can erase the later `config_changed()` warning, and previewing a fatal/partial plan can change future `not_reached` versus `no_record` reporting.
findings.suggested_fix: Snapshot the complete ledger before planning and restore it for dry runs, or avoid all ledger mutation/saves on the dry-run path.

findings.title: Digest compatibility hides an accounting-model migration in legacy ledgers
findings.evidence: The new `retry.killed_budget: 2` is omitted from the digest, legacy task records are loaded with absent fields defaulting `attempts_killed` to zero, and abnormal retryable records now charge `attempts_killed` rather than `attempts_record`.
findings.why_wrong: The pre-change runner charged every final retryable record, including abnormal ends, to `attempts_record`; old ledgers therefore contain counts with different semantics and no killed-axis history. Matching their digest silently resumes them under the new model, allowing different retry/settlement behavior without a migration or warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Version the accounting model in the ledger/digest and migrate old counters explicitly, or require an explicit legacy-ledger upgrade/replan instead of treating the new default as behavior-compatible.

findings.title: DIGEST_COMPAT_DEFAULTS claims killed_budget:2 reproduces pre-key behaviour; it does not
findings.why_wrong: Omitting killed_budget:2 from the digest makes a new runner resume an old output root without a config-changed warning, but pre-key builds charged ABNORMAL_END×RETRY_RECORD to record, not killed. Mid-sweep ledgers that already have attempts_record from kill-shaped ends are then continued under a different axis with attempts_killed starting at 0, so settlement timing and possible final statuses diverge silently across the runner-version boundary the digest claims is identical.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop killed_budget from DIGEST_COMPAT_DEFAULTS (accept re-plan warnings on upgrade), or bump a digest-visible runner_accounting_epoch when the 6A model changes, or migrate old ledgers by copying kill-attributed record charges into attempts_killed on load.
